contexts.description: Top-level Next.js application shell: root layout, global CSS, React context providers, and all page-route entry points for every screen. It wires the app together without containing feature logic, and bootstraps the server-side instrumentation hook.
contexts.name: app-routing

contexts.description: Project-level build and development tooling: Next.js config, TypeScript config, ESLint config, Vitest config, demo-data build script, structure-check script, infra Cloud Run README, the Belay CLI wrapper, trust policy YAML files, and the adopt-belay skill instructions.
contexts.name: build-tooling

contexts.description: The embedded PGlite database: schema migrations, repositories (fleet, work, ledger, pairing, pollState), views that project fleet/maturity/needsYou/tasks from raw tables, seed loaders, and the index entry point. This is the single source of truth for all persisted Belay state within a running instance.
contexts.name: database-index

contexts.description: The domain model, hooks, UI widgets, and data loader for the door landing screen. Covers geometric camera/fit calculations, city layout, quality scoring, and the count-up animation hooks. Feeds into the visual scene components.
contexts.name: door-data-model

contexts.description: The animated cyberpunk landing screen ('Afterlife front door') that greets users when they first open Belay. It renders an SVG city scene with camera, district, beam, and ground layers driven by CSS animations and React. It depends on door model geometry and the door data loader.
contexts.name: door-visual-scene

contexts.api_surface: CLI: belay prove | gate | ledger | tripwire | envelope
contexts.description: The Belay engine CLI entry point and its five commands (envelope, gate, ledger, prove, tripwire). Core utilities cover argument parsing, ULID generation, file I/O, type definitions, and version. This is the local binary invoked by CI pipelines to evaluate proofs and emit gate decisions.
contexts.name: engine-core-cli

contexts.description: The proof evaluation core: six proof-type implementations (citedDiff, exploitTest, linkedEvidence, rerunStats, weakening, stubs), gate and tripwire decision logic, diff/JUnit/trace parsers, and policy loading with glob-pattern matching. This library converts raw CI artifacts into structured proof verdicts.
contexts.name: engine-proof-logic

contexts.description: Business logic, view-model, and React hooks for the Fleet screen. Computes column definitions, project groupings, filtering/sorting lists, smart filter presets, inspector shape, and 'needs-you' counts per project. Also contains context-menu and toolbar-menu model factories.
contexts.name: fleet-model-hooks

contexts.description: The Fleet screen: a sortable, groupable table showing every GitLab project and its current security-tier scores. Components cover the table, sidebar, legend, tier popover, status header, and inspector panels for groups and projects. Data is loaded server-side via loadFleetData.
contexts.name: fleet-overview-ui

contexts.description: GitLab CI pipeline definitions for the eight Belay agent flows (guardrail, cra, qa, medic, patcher, gardener) plus reusable CI component templates (proof-engine, tier-gate, ledger-append, maturity-scan, tripwire, flow-dispatch) and their supporting shell scripts. Together these wired into a target project's .gitlab-ci.yml to activate proof-carrying agents.
contexts.name: gitlab-ci-flows

contexts.api_surface: GitLab REST: /groups, /projects, /merge_requests, /jobs, /vulnerabilities; GitLab GraphQL: namespace, group-members
contexts.description: Server-side GitLab adapter: wraps the glab CLI and GitLab REST/GraphQL APIs to read groups, projects, MRs, CI jobs, vulnerabilities, and ledger files, and to write proof notes, gate decisions, and ledger commits. The fake server provides a hermetic in-process stub for integration tests.
contexts.name: gitlab-server-adapter

contexts.description: Business logic and state management for the Ladder screen. Covers tier promotion rules, dock plan evaluation, class view rows and filters, timeline sorting, a simulated clock, and the state reducer for staged tier-edit actions. Also includes data loaders, ledger seed, and keyboard/menu hooks.
contexts.name: ladder-model

contexts.description: The Ladder screen: a table of security classes (project categories) showing their current tier level, last move, and promotion history. Includes a policy lozenge for filtering by tier, a sidebar for tier/class counts, a dock for staged tier-edit commands, and an inspector with grant/write/move sections.
contexts.name: ladder-view

contexts.description: Shared runtime utilities and TypeScript schemas. Covers tier constants, keyboard hotkey registration, text-size settings store, time/plural formatters, version, the demo data bundle (belay-demo.json + loaders), and Zod-style schema definitions for ledger entries, proofs, stages, tiers, and CRA objects used across server and client.
contexts.name: lib-schemas

contexts.description: Domain model, data loaders, and hooks for the Maturity screen. Covers crag geometry calculations, rung and step logic, credit-flow state machine, reducer, filtering/sorting view models, and seed data for proposals and stage evidence. Key dependency for the maturity UI.
contexts.name: maturity-scan-model

contexts.description: The Maturity screen: a visual 'climbing crag' metaphor showing a project's security-stage progress across multiple routes (tracks). Components cover the crag SVG backdrop with animated route/rope rendering, the gaps-table for missing coverage, a legend, and a send-sheet overlay for submitting proposals.
contexts.name: maturity-scan-ui

contexts.description: The Monitor screen: a real-time event feed that displays agent decisions, proof verdicts, and guardrail outcomes across projects. Shows a leads strip, decision inspector with per-beat breakdown, totals, and status bar. Data is loaded server-side and driven by a polling beat model.
contexts.name: monitor-dashboard

contexts.description: The Needs You screen: the primary action queue that surfaced agent decisions requiring human approval (promote, readmit, CRA sign-off, etc.). The band component shows a 24-h rail with evidence strips and grade ladders; the decisions table lists pending items grouped by type with countdown urgency signals.
contexts.name: needs-you-band-table

contexts.description: Complete domain model, data fixtures, and hooks for the Needs You screen. Covers the outbox command reducer, clock/grade urgency logic, row grouping and history, action dispatch, menu model, and all fixture seed data (cra, gaps, promote, readmit, runner). The reducer ties the full action dispatch loop together.
contexts.name: needs-you-model

contexts.description: Inspector, toolbar, outbox, and shared mark components for the Needs You screen. The inspector renders per-item detail panels (CRA, gap, promote, readmit, runner). The outbox drawer stages and previews write-back commands before they are dispatched to GitLab. Shared glyphs (DecisionGlyph, GradeChip, MoveMarks) are used across panels.
contexts.name: needs-you-panels

contexts.description: Server-side data source abstraction: a DataSource interface with demo and live implementations, config loading, boot-time initialization, snapshot/narrow helpers, and live-clock polling. The demo source serves static JSON; the live source polls PGlite for fresh data. Also includes the ledger import pipeline (parse + importLedger).
contexts.name: server-data-sources

contexts.api_surface: Next.js Server Actions: promoteClass, revokeClass, submitCra, submitGap, editTier
contexts.description: Next.js Server Actions that execute write-back operations to GitLab on behalf of the user (promote, revoke, gap, CRA, tier-edit). The actions layer validates intents, builds GitLab plan objects via per-action plan builders, and dispatches them through the GitLab adapter. Also tracks command run history.
contexts.name: server-ledger-actions

contexts.description: Background polling engine that periodically fetches new CI events from GitLab and writes derived state into the PGlite index. Parse stage extracts proof blocks, guardrail verdicts, labels, and trailers from raw job logs. Derive stage computes tier rollups, readmit eligibility, task records, and policy snapshots.
contexts.name: server-poller

contexts.description: The Settings screen (keyboard shortcuts, text size control, about section) and the Kit gallery screen (a developer component showcase listing controls, overlays, shell, status, table, and viz components). Both are lightweight feature screens that reference shared UI primitives.
contexts.name: settings-kit-screens

contexts.description: Inspector panel and shared primitive components for the Setup screen. Covers per-capability, per-track, and per-step inspector panels that show probe age, dependency rows, gate rows, and 'needs-you' auxiliary info. Shared glyphs (CapGlyph, Spinner, DepRow, GateRow) are reused across all panel types.
contexts.name: setup-inspector-panel

contexts.description: The Setup screen: an interactive dependency graph ('Unlock Map') showing the eight CI capability tracks and how enabling each one unlocks downstream steps. Provides a toolbar for onboarding progress, status/legend overlays, and an SVG edge-layer connecting track/step/cap nodes.
contexts.name: setup-map-view

contexts.description: Data, hooks, and domain model for the Setup screen. The setup flow reducer manages arm/probe state per track, a graph model (appGraph, edges, hot) computes the unlock dependency DAG, and wording helpers produce human-readable probe descriptions. Data loaders supply capability metadata and step timing.
contexts.name: setup-model

contexts.description: Primitive interactive controls (Button, Checkbox, Kbd, Lozenge, ObjectLink, Spacer, toolbar controls) and the icon system (SVG glyph registry + Icon wrapper). These are the lowest-level building blocks consumed by every feature screen.
contexts.name: shared-controls-icons

contexts.description: Floating overlays (menu, popover, sheet, toast, help button) and the shared inspector block primitives (DiffBlock, Stats, CommandBlock, InspectorHeader, InspectorSection, KeyValue, UntrustedText). These are used across every feature's inspector panel and context-menu interactions.
contexts.name: shared-overlays-inspector

contexts.description: Application window chrome: the sidebar nav with traffic lights and nav links, the toolbar/inspector/statusbar layout bars, the bottom drawer, dock (command shortcut display), pane scroll, and global CSS tokens. This is the outermost layer every feature screen is wrapped in.
contexts.name: shared-shell-nav

contexts.description: Shared data-display primitives: the generic OutlineTable with row navigation and sort hooks, visualization components (DayStrip, ProofBar, RungGlyph, StageMeter, StageTicks), status indicators (TierChip, TierMark, StateGlyph, HonestyChip, NeedsYouBadge, FeedAge), and the Card surface. Consumed across fleet, ladder, maturity, and task screens.
contexts.name: shared-table-viz-status

contexts.description: Business logic for the Task screen. Covers task building from the ledger, verdict equation evaluation, replay slice, exhibit extraction, docket filtering, court/ties layout, and page-level fact loading. Also includes the full seed dataset (q4–qc detail files) used for demo rendering.
contexts.name: task-verdict-model

contexts.description: The Task screen: a deep-dive view for a single CI proof event showing the court (claims vs checks), verdict equation, receipt chain of evidence, docket of sub-events, and a replay button. Components cover the court card grid, ties geometry, equation terms, and the inspector with exhibits and ledger rows.
contexts.name: task-verdict-view

contexts.description: Replay engine, derived view-model, and hooks for the Theater screen. The replay store manages scrub position and frame snapshots; derive functions project answers, climb progress, and time labels per frame. Inspector components (BeatInspector, LedgerSection, NeedsSection) consume these projections for sidebar display.
contexts.name: theater-replay-model

contexts.description: The Theater screen: a full playback UI for replaying a CI agent run beat-by-beat. Shows a stage board with pitch/answers, a capability wall, a side rail with stage rows and CRA blocks, a takes sidebar, and a transport control bar. The replay store drives frame-by-frame scrubbing across agent pipeline snapshots.
contexts.name: theater-view
